cards.text: Job, the man who lost so much, is still talking, right where he left off with his friends. And now he goes somewhere NOBODY saw coming: underground. 'Surely there is a mine for silver and a place where gold is refined.'

cards.question: Silver has its mine, and gold has its place to be refined. Iron, Job says, is taken from the ___.

cards.text: Then Job turns to the miner, who digs for ore in the deepest darkness. Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer begging for a little light, and this man goes down there ON PURPOSE.

cards.question: True or false: Job says the darkness deep down in the mine is too much for the miner.
The miner needs a place to cut his shaft. Where does Job say he cuts it?

cards.text: Job says, 'Far from men he dangles and sways.' That's me hanging off the top shelf of my bakery by my mustache, gold base swinging, reaching for the sprinkles.
Then Job points out something wild about the ground. Up top, the earth gives food, but down below it's transformed as by fire.

cards.question: Down in the rocks under the earth, what does Job say is waiting for the miner?

cards.text: That path down to the treasure is so hidden, even the sharpest eyes in the sky have never seen it, and the proudest beasts have never set foot on it.

cards.question: Job names a bird whose eye has never seen the miner's path and a beast that has never prowled over it. Which two?

cards.text: Meanwhile, the miner is going to WORK. He strikes the flint and overturns mountains at their base, and friend, I can't flip one cookie without breaking it.

cards.question: The miner hews out channels in the rocks. True or false: Job says the miner's eyes spot every treasure down there.

cards.text: He even stops up the sources of the streams. WHOLE STREAMS, friend. Stopped up!

cards.question: The miner stops up the streams so he can bring what is hidden to ___.
From silver mines to dark shafts to stopped-up streams, what is Job showing about people?

answers.text: They'll go to great lengths for hidden treasure
They're too afraid to dig deep into the earth
They leave the earth's treasure where it lies

cards.text: Then Job flips the whole thing around. People can dig silver, gold and sapphires out of the dark, 'But where can wisdom be found, and where does understanding dwell?'

cards.question: After all that talk of treasure, Job says no man can know wisdom's ___.
True or false: Job says wisdom can be found in the land of the living.

cards.text: The ocean depths say, 'It is not in me,' while the sea declares, 'It is not with me.' The sea is the junk drawer of the whole world, EVERYTHING ends up down there, and even IT says nope.

cards.question: Wisdom can't be found down deep. True or false: Job says it can be bought with gold.

cards.text: Then Job lines up the finest treasures on earth next to wisdom: gold of Ophir, onyx, sapphire, crystal, coral, quartz, rubies and topaz from Cush.

cards.question: How do all those treasures measure up next to wisdom?

answers.text: None of them can compare to it
Rubies come the closest to it
Together they can match its price

cards.text: So Job asks again where wisdom comes from. It's hidden from the eyes of every living thing, even the birds of the air.

cards.question: Even Abaddon and Death have something to say about wisdom. What is it?

answers.text: They've heard a rumor about it

cards.text: A RUMOR. Abaddon and Death themselves, and all they've got is something somebody mentioned in the group chat.

cards.question: Nobody alive has it, but Job knows who does: 'But God ___ its way, and He knows its place.'
Why does God know where wisdom is when nobody else does?

answers.text: He sees everything under the heavens
The ocean told Him where it was
He dug it up from the mountains

cards.text: Job takes it back to when God fixed the weight of the wind and measured out the waters, and set a limit for the rain and a path for the thunderbolt. Friend, I measure flour for ONE batch and still get it wrong.

cards.question: Back when God set up the wind and the rain, what did He do with wisdom?

answers.text: He looked at it and established it
He buried it under the deep sea
He handed it to the birds of the air

cards.text: And then God speaks to man and tells him what wisdom is.

cards.question: What does God tell man that wisdom is?
True or false: God tells man that to turn away from evil is understanding.

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend. Job's not done talking, so keep your apron on.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: the statement about stopping the streams, "WHOLE STREAMS, friend." and "Stopped up!"

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question depends on "all those treasures," but the treasures are identified only on the preceding story card, which is no longer on screen. The question needs to identify the treasures itself.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what.

findings.problem: This story card only repeats and jokes about the rumor answer just given on card 9. It adds no new passage content and functions as a standalone recap and reaction.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: "Nobody alive has it" does not identify what "it" is. The question relies on earlier cards rather than naming wisdom in its own context.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: "Nobody alive has it" stretches the passage. Job says wisdom is not found in the land of the living and is hidden from every living thing's eyes, not that no living person possesses wisdom; verse 28 identifies the fear of the Lord as wisdom. A wording such as "Nobody alive can find it" would stay within the text.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.
